chunks: 5512 - Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Ali ibn Ri'ab, who said:

I asked Abā al-Ḥasan Mūsā عليه السلام about a man between whom and me was kinship, who died and left young children, and left male and female slaves, and did not leave a bequest. So what do you see regarding one who buys from them a slave-girl and takes her as an umm walad? And what do you see regarding their sale?
So he said: “If they have a guardian who undertakes their affairs, sells on their behalf, and looks after them, he is rewarded concerning them.”
I said: “Then what do you see regarding one who buys from them a slave-girl and takes her as an umm walad?”

He said: “There is no harm in that if the custodian responsible for them, looking to what benefits them, sells on their behalf. And they have no right to go back on what the custodian responsible for them, looking to what benefits them, has done.”

key_terms.أَوْلَادًا صِغَارًا: young children who are minors and unable to manage their own estate
key_terms.أُمَّ وَلَدٍ: a slave-concubine who bears a child to her master
key_terms.النَّاظِرُ: the one who considers and oversees what is beneficial for them
key_terms.الْجَارِيَةَ: a female slave from the estate in question
key_terms.الْقَيِّمُ: the custodian or manager appointed over their affairs
key_terms.وَلِيٌّ: a guardian with legal responsibility over the minors’ affairs
key_terms.يُصْلِحُهُمْ: what serves their welfare and best interest

ai.seo_question: Can a guardian sell the property of orphaned minor heirs, and is such a sale legally valid?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about the property of minor heirs after the death of a relative who left no bequest. It establishes that a guardian or custodian may sell from their estate when acting for their welfare, and such a sale is valid and binding. It also permits the purchase of a slave-girl from that estate, including taking her as an umm walad, so long as the transaction is carried out by the responsible guardian in the minors’ best interest.
